category_title: Non-verbal male students with classic autism who struggle with functional communication and use tactile tracing for letter recognition
minimal_context: The student is using an iPad to trace letters of the alphabet during a language arts lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our language arts lesson. Please trace the letter on the iPad.

STUDENT: (Slides his finger across the tablet, tracing along the screen to practice writing the letter.)

TUTOR: Now let's answer the comprehension question. Use your Springboard Lite device to tell me which letter you just traced.

STUDENT: (Looks at the Springboard Lite device but does not use it to communicate the answer.)

TUTOR: What do you think? You can also just tell me the letter.

STUDENT: (Remains silent, showing difficulty using natural speech to meet the communication need, and pushes the Springboard Lite device away without using it functionally.)

options.A: Terminate the demands and remove the Springboard Lite device for 10 seconds.
options.B: Provide an iPad app that offers instant rewards with audio and text.
options.C: Ask the student the name of the letter, prompting, "This one, you know it, it's in your name."
options.D: Ask the student to verbally describe the form of the letter he just traced.
